requestedIdentity.fitHypothesis: Same artist, release and 136 BPM plus source-described rolling percussion/pads make this the strongest same-room continuation hypothesis; actual perceived energy continuity remains unmeasured.

measured: 136 BPM from Beatport exact artist-track metadata
evidence.attributedDescription: Inigo Kennedy / Asymmetric describes The Witching Hour as classic Asymmetric, with rolling bass-heavy percussion against yearnful pads that tip upward occasionally. This is attributed source evidence, not direct listening or raw-audio analysis.
evidence.listenerEvidence: The listener rejected the prior four-track opening because each track felt like an energy shift; any new Track 2 must therefore prioritize same-room continuity above novelty.
evidence.craftConvention: A same-release, same-tempo continuation can reduce production-context variance, but it cannot by itself prove perceived-energy continuity.
